full_judgment: 4. The appellate court below found that the vendor of the case land opposite party No. 4 filed a petition on 12.5.69 to C.O.(Rev.), Kishoregonj for splitting up of his jams in respect of some land appertaining to S.A. Khatian No. 18 and 53 Tahsilder submitted a proposal recommending the splitting up. The Revenue Officer concerned allowed the splitting up of the jama by order dated 10.2.70. The present Misc. case u/s 96 was filed on 31.1.70. The learned Additional District Judge did not consider the order of splitting up passed by the Revenue Officer on 10.2.70 as a proper order because he found that there is no evidence that the pre-emptor opposite party No. 1 was made a party in the proceeding. There is also no evidence to show that all the co-sharers were served with notices in the said proceeding. As such both the courts below held that there was no splitting up of jama according to law.
